Your spoil isn't the cost. The water in it is.
Liquid drilling waste has to go somewhere. Vacuum truck, cart it away wet, pay by the load.

Most of what you're paying to haul is water. The slurry is heavy and wet, and it fills a truck fast.

Turn it solid and the whole job changes. Liquid and solid waste aren't classed the same, or priced the same. Pass the paint filter test and your spoil counts as a solid, so you can skip it, landfill it, or on the right site spread it back across the ground instead of carting it anywhere.

So the real question isn't how to truck the slurry out. It's whether you need to haul it at all.
How many wet loads did your last urban job truck out?

Eco Dry turns your wet spoil into a solid you can stack.
It's a dry powder. Pour it into your spoil pit or return fluid, mix it through with an excavator bucket, and the slurry firms up in minutes.

No pumps, no service crew, no waiting. You load the solid into a skip instead of a vacuum truck. On the right job, you spread it back across the site and it never leaves at all.

That's fewer truck movements and lower disposal cost. On a tight urban job, that's the difference.

Dose runs about a quarter to one percent by weight. The wetter the waste, the more you need, so for the really sloppy stuff give the team a call.
What's spoil disposal costing you per job right now?

PPE guidance stays on the SDS/spec, not the post. No fabricated specs or stories. Seasonal note: Eco Dry normally leans summer, but chosen now to break the Carry Flow/Filter Low repeat and because it's the overdue strategic-growth product. **On-site redistribution line added from your 2026-06-15 customer case** ("spread it back across the site, never leaves at all"). Kept qualified ("on the right job") because on-site reuse of solidified spoil is subject to state EPA rules and contamination conditions — captured in specs/eco-dry.md with a NEEDS VERIFICATION flag.
